interpretation.reproduced: The observed ASINs are reproducible: observations #1-#4 (2026-11-17, then arena-23d7ed19, arena-82d39deb and arena-c2123b9c on 2026-11-20) agreed 5/5, and the listing re-reads by arena-70bd2fcc (S30-S34) and arena/1c6908d1 (S36) confirmed every observed listing still serves the recorded page. The SHORT LINKS are a different story: two independent re-resolution passes on 2026-11-20 (arena/1c6908d1 -> FLG-030; b0920c92 -> FLG-031, S37) both found four of the five short links landing on the Amazon home page, with only B0f3GKalj still resolving to a product. So: the observed_* product records are reproducible; the submitted short links' behaviour is not stable over hours.
interpretation.what_reproduction_does_not_prove: Every final URL ever observed carries lv=shuf (shuffle) and plpRedirect=mhFallback (listing-page fallback) - a fallback route, not a canonical resolution of the submitted token, which is why the intended_* fields stay blank (FLG-009, FLG-029). The divergence passes (FLG-030, FLG-031) add a second reason: the short links did not all resolve to product pages on the two most recent passes. Nothing here says the short links are invalid - FLG-003 remains open and unresolved.
interpretation.operational_consequence: The reader-facing links on this site are NOT the submitted short links. They are built from the observed ASINs as direct https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> URLs. All five were re-opened directly on 2026-11-20 as a control in observation #6 (S37) and every one still served the product page and breadcrumb recorded in data/products.json. So the published links are unaffected by the short-link behaviour; what needs the owner's attention is confirming the intended destination for each product (Q-02) and the one-link Associates test (FLG-002).
